A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CLIPoint3D and contain readable methods, equations, figures, tables and supplementary analyses. Appendix renumbering and layout changes can be matched reliably, including the retained algorithm.

before.justification: v1 reports original adaptation results on PointDA-10 and GraspNetPC-10, together with component ablations, sensitivity analyses and embedding visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports handcrafted-prompt comparison results in Table A4.

M1.justification: The CLIPoint3D prompt-generation modules, LoRA adaptation, entropy-guided view selection, alignment losses and inference procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 is unchanged apart from formatting and placement.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PointDA-10 and GraspNetPC-10 domains, categories and transfer directions. The new handcrafted-prompt comparison uses existing GraspNetPC-10 tasks without extending dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table A4 adds a Handcrafted comparator to the LLM-attribute comparison in v1 Table 11. Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen2.5-14B, Phi-4 and GPT-5 remain, as do the comparator sets in the other experiments.

E3.justification: The reported splits, accuracy metric and training settings remain unchanged, including 64 shots per class, 50 epochs and batch size 32. The handcrafted comparator uses the existing transfer evaluation. Newly identified model variants in appendix captions clarify existing experiments rather than establish changed settings.

E4.justification: Table A4 extends the existing LLM-attribute ablation with a handcrafted-prompt control, adding evidence about the benefit of generated attributes. It also supplies illustrative attribute snippets for a drill machine. Existing loss, rank, prompt-length, backbone and view analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over three runs in Section 4. Neither adds seed information, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 Table A4 newly reports handcrafted-prompt accuracies of 93.5, 81.6, 77.9 and 94.8 across the four GraspNetPC-10 transfers, averaging 87.0%. The existing LLM scores, including GPT-5's 92.2% average, and the other matched tables and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives and Section 3.3 generalization-bound argument, including Equations 15–17, are retained. No additional or revised proof, assumption or derivation appears in the appendices.

C1.justification: The first CLIP-based few-shot 3D adaptation claim, four principal contributions and accuracy-efficiency claims retain their scope. The revised conclusion repeats the 3–16% improvement claim already present in v1's abstract.

C2.justification: The interpretations of domain alignment, prompting, PEFT and sensitivity results remain substantively unchanged. The removed conclusion sentence describes a prospective self-refinement extension, without revising an interpretation or limitation of the reported work.

D1.justification: v2 specifies a single 80 GB A100 GPU and identifies the CLIPoint3D-V/B variants used in existing appendix experiments. Table A4 adds prompt snippets. The abstract replaces the direct code-repository link with project-page access information; the PDFs do not establish a change in actual resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 removes the specific discussion of COSMo's open-set multi-target adaptation, while retaining its reference and citing it generally in the introduction. The cited-work set and broader positioning against CLIP-based recognition and conventional 3D adaptation remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording, affiliation, contact and acknowledgment edits, shortens the conclusion and removes the main-text supplementary roadmap. It adds an introductory sentence and section label to the supplementary contents, shifting subsequent appendix labels without substantially reorganizing the narrative.

P2.justification: Table 11 becomes Table A4, with methods transposed into rows, an added handcrafted row and an attribute-snippet column. Appendix displays receive A-prefixed numbering and more specific captions. Algorithm 1 shares the final page with the LLM comparison and discussion; existing diagrams and plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The handcrafted control in Table A4 strengthens the evidence for generated attributes, reporting 87.0% average accuracy alongside the retained 92.2% GPT-5 result. Explicit ablation variants, prompt examples and GPU information improve experimental clarity and reproducibility. These are useful, limited gains while the core method, theory and previous results remain unchanged.
